title: Use-case set
description: Contract for docs/USE_CASES.md, the use-case SSOT. A use case is what an ACTOR wants to accomplish, and the features that accomplishing it requires. Enforced by scripts/check-use-cases.mjs (UC-NN, #2480 wave 8). Shape taken from a real product's matrix rather than invented: the fields are those a shipped use-case matrix already carried, which is also what forma's traceability lens renders.

useCases.description: Every use case the product claims. An empty list is legitimate and distinct from an absent file: the first means nothing is claimed, the second means nothing is codified.

actor.description: WHO wants this. A use case with no actor is a feature description wearing a use case's name — the actor is what makes it a claim about someone's world rather than about the code.

goal.description: What the actor accomplishes, in their terms. Not the mechanism.

featureIds.description: The features this use case requires, which the gate resolves against the feature matrix. `minItems: 1` is the load-bearing constraint: a use case demanding no feature is a promise with nothing behind it, and it is precisely what an unmaintained matrix accumulates.

journeyIds.description: Optional journeys this use case belongs to. Not resolved — journeys are a product-side vocabulary this contract does not own, and validating a reference into a namespace it cannot see would be a false red.

prdRef.description: Optional upward anchor to the requirement's origin, e.g. `PRD §3`. Format-only, never dereferenced — the same treatment FEATURE_MATRIX's source_ref gives a non-canonical anchor, and for the same reason: a gate that reaches outside its own tree fails when the network does, not when the document is wrong.

status.description: The ladder. `linked` means every featureId resolves; `exercised` additionally means a tabletop scenario walks it. Both are gate-checked, so neither can be claimed by typing it.
